Subject: APAC maintenance window — inference runtime harmonization (driver + NIC firmware)

Hi Julia / Acme ops team,

We wanted to give advance notice of a planned maintenance window targeting APAC inference capacity (apac-southeast1) to harmonize runtime drivers and NIC firmware across our Dedicated and Private clusters. This is a coordinated change that reduces kernel/firmware divergence and prevents transient runtime regressions we've observed during mixed-driver schedules.

Planned window:
- Start: 2027-03-19 00:30 UTC (2027-03-19 08:30 +08:00)
- End: 2027-03-19 04:30 UTC (2027-03-19 12:30 +08:00)
- Affected: apac-southeast1 clusters in Dedicated and Private modes (hosted API unaffected unless routed to Dedicated capacity)

What to expect:
- We will perform rolling restarts by rack to apply a driver + NIC firmware harmonization bundle. Each rack will be drained, updated, and returned to service.
- Typical per-node interruption: brief (target < 90 seconds) token-generation interruption while the workload is drained and the process restarted.
- We will use smart-routing fallback: critical customer traffic can be routed to eu-west temporarily if configured in your routing policy.

Attachments: maintenance plan (schedule, rollback criteria, and runbook) attached.

Immediate asks:
1) Let us know if you require a blackout period or if you cannot accept any service interruptions during that UTC window.
2) Confirm whether you want automatic fallback to eu-west enabled for your organization (we can flip this for Acme on the morning of the 19th).

Point people:
- Engineering runbook lead: Markus Klein (markus_klein@redwood.ai)
- Customer liaison / scheduling: Soojin Lee (soojin_lee@redwood.ai)
- Account executive: Monica Patel (monica_patel@redwood.ai)

We'll post real-time updates to https://status.redwood.example.com during the window.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Alex / Acme team — quick technical notes to address your questions: 

- The ~90s interruption target is per-node during the drain/restart; we drain connection pools so inflight requests are allowed to finish when possible. A small fraction of requests active at the exact moment of process termination may receive 5xx; our routing policy will retry automatically for idempotent operations.

- Rollback criteria (high level) — if we see a sustained 5xx increase above 1.5x baseline across more than 3 consecutive 5-minute buckets for a single rack, we will trigger an immediate rollback to the prior driver image for that rack and stop the window. Full rollback steps are in the attached runbook.

- No application-level changes required on your side. If you want to avoid any risk for the critical checkout traffic, we recommend enabling smart-routing to eu-west for the duration (we can enable this for Acme and test at 07:30 UTC on the 19th).

Runbook excerpt: drain -> quiesce -> apply firmware -> restart runtime -> validation tests (health + perf) -> un-drain.

If you'd like, we can set up a 20-minute pre-window call at 07:45 UTC for quick alignment.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Engineering Lead, Runtime Reliability

- Post-maintenance validation: all health checks green, performance test suite within 3% of baseline.

- Post-maintenance logs: post_maintenance_logs_20270319.zip (attached)
